Reproducibility
Where possible, the code that accompanies my published papers is released alongside the working-paper version. If you are looking for replication materials for a specific paper and cannot find them, please email me.

title: Teaching
text:
At Bocconi I have developed and currently direct multiple courses that integrate Data Science, AI, and computational methods into the MSc. and BSc. curricula in Accounting and AI. The aim is to make students fluent in advanced analytical techniques — from Natural Language Processing to Blockchain fundamentals — so they can lead in data-rich accounting and finance environments.
In 2023–2024 I received the Bocconi Teaching Award for Innovation for the course Introduction to Blockchain.

title: Teaching
text:
Current courses — Bocconi University

Big Data for Business Decisions
MSc. Elective
Advanced data-science methods applied to managerial and accounting problems: from data wrangling at scale to predictive modeling and the use of textual and unstructured data in business decisions.


Statistical and Computational Methods in Accounting
BSc. in Artificial Intelligence — Elective
Statistical learning, computational statistics, and modern programming practices applied to accounting data. Connects the foundations of statistical inference to the analytical workflows used in research and industry.


Introduction to Blockchain
BSc. Elective
A hands-on introduction to distributed ledger technologies: cryptographic primitives, consensus, smart contracts, and the accounting/auditing implications of on-chain data. Bocconi Teaching Award for Innovation, 2023–2024.

title: Francesco Grossetti
text:
I am an Assistant Professor of Accounting Analytics and Data Science at the Department of Accounting at Bocconi University, a Fellow at the Bocconi Institute for Data Science and Analytics, and a member of the Bocconi Digital Transformation and AI Committee.
My research sits at the intersection of Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, and empirical finance. I use large-scale textual and multimodal financial data to study corporate disclosure and its consequences — including firm tax outcomes and investor reactions to multi-dimensional financial narratives. Methodologically, I draw on statistical learning and computational statistics, with a focus on stochastic processes for sequential data, which lets me model how corporate information evolves over time (disclosure cascades, topic model identification, and more).
My work has appeared in the Review of Accounting Studies, the Journal of Machine Learning Research, the Journal of Accounting and Public Policy, and other outlets. I am an Editorial Board member of Accounting in Europe (2026–2029) and Scientific Program Coordinator of the 4th Bocconi Accounting Symposium (June 2026).
